**Bahrain**,[[a]](#cite_note-17) officially the **Kingdom of Bahrain**,[[b]](#cite_note-18) is an [island country](/wiki/Island_country "Island country") in [West Asia](/wiki/West_Asia "West Asia"). Situated near the western shore of the [Persian Gulf](/wiki/Persian_Gulf "Persian Gulf") and latitudinally about two-thirds the shore's length from the north, the country comprises a small [archipelago](/wiki/Archipelago "Archipelago") of 33 natural islands and an additional 50 [artificial islands](/wiki/Artificial_island "Artificial island"), centered on [Bahrain Island](/wiki/Bahrain_Island "Bahrain Island"), which makes up around 80 percent of the country's landmass. Bahrain is situated between [Qatar](/wiki/Qatar "Qatar") and the northeastern coast of [Saudi Arabia](/wiki/Saudi_Arabia "Saudi Arabia"), to which it is connected by the [King Fahd Causeway](/wiki/King_Fahd_Causeway "King Fahd Causeway"). The oil market was tight in the early 1970s, which reduced the risks for OPEC members in nationalising their oil production. One of the major fears for OPEC members was that nationalisation would cause a steep decline in the price of oil. This prompted a wave of nationalisations in countries such as Libya, Algeria, Iraq, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela. With greater control over oil production decisions and amid high oil prices, OPEC members unilaterally raised oil prices in 1973, prompting the 1973 oil crisis.[[56]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColgan2021The_Rise_of_OPEC,_pp._79–85-56)
